A1.justification: Both 27-page PDFs describe the same research, renamed from DexDiffuser to DexHandDiff. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete Appendices A–F support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4.pdf reports original Adroit and Shadow Hand simulation results, including task success rates, ghost-state measurements, ablations and control frequencies in Tables 2–7.

after.justification: v6.pdf retains these original simulation results in Tables 2–7 and the qualitative demonstrations in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The joint state-action diffusion model, dynamics guidance, contact-dependent phases and LLM guidance-generation pipeline are unchanged, as are Appendix F's code samples. The rename and constraint-energy explanation edits do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Door, Pen, Hammer, Relocate and Block tasks with the same goal-shift scenarios. Door reversal, hemisphere shifts, partial nail driving and Appendix C's dynamic pen-goal tracking are already present in v4.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains both Diffuser variants, Decision Diffuser, Diffusion Policy and the proposed method's discrete variant. Table 3 retains Diffuser and Conditional DP with the same task-dependent implementations. Renamed entries represent the same methods.

E3.justification: Training distributions, goal conditioning, evaluation metrics and experimental settings match. This includes 90-degree-only door training, normalized L2 ghost-state measurements and the training and inference configurations in Appendix D.

E4.justification: Both retain the ghost-state analysis, LLM-guidance comparison and component ablations in Tables 4–6. The failure analysis in Section 6.1 and qualitative case studies in Appendix C are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report three tries for ten random seeds and the same standard-deviation reporting in Tables 2–3. The three-try ghost-state evaluation and ten-try control-frequency measurement are unchanged; no statistical procedure is added.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 2–7 match after method renaming. For example, Table 2 retains averages of 59.2% for the proposed method and 29.5% for Diffuser with Guided Sampling, while Table 3 retains 70.7%. The qualitative findings also match.

T1.justification: Section 5.1 changes the asserted Dirac-delta characterization: v4 assigns it to εfinger after Equation 16, whereas v6 assigns it to εpenalty after Equation 14 and explicitly invokes Equation 11. This is a limited mathematical-explanation revision; the numbered equations and Appendix A's theorems and proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same interaction-aware, goal-adaptive planning contributions, text-to-reward extension claim and headline performance claims. The method rename does not alter their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Both retain the explanations of ghost states, training-distribution bias and the guidance-versus-in-domain-performance tradeoff. Vision-based sensing and real-world deployment remain future work, with no added applicability qualification or limitation.

D1.justification: Appendix D retains the architecture, optimization settings, planning horizons, guidance scales and RTX 3090 training information. Appendices E–F retain identical prompts and generated code. The supplied project link is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds citations to RoboScript, G3Flow and Plot2Code, removes Object-centric Dexterous Manipulation from Human Motion Data, and adds a reference to this same paper under its former title. RoboCodeX remains in a grouped citation. The broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: DexDiffuser becomes DexHandDiff throughout the title, prose and supplement. Short passages in Sections 2 and 5.1 are edited, and the acknowledgements add Jockey Club support. The section structure and most wording remain unchanged.

P2.justification: All seven figures and seven tables are retained. Captions and table labels reflect the rename, with local spacing, column-width and text-flow adjustments; Equation 15 moves onto page 6. The visual evidence is unchanged.

improvement.justification: Consistent use of DexHandDiff resolves v4's mismatch with names already printed in Figures 1 and 3 and distinguishes the method from the separately cited DexDiffuser grasping work. Defining H at its first use also improves readability. These are limited clarity gains: experiments, proofs and implementation material are preserved, while the revised Dirac-delta assertion remains unsupported by Equation 11.
